children: The Indian rupee opened lower against the US dollar on September 24 amid renewed rise in oil prices and a broadly firmer dollar on account of growing US rate hike expectations.
The rupee opened 9 paise lower at 95.83 per dollar, compared with Wednesday’s close of 95.74.
According to Finrex, as US yields rose to 5.13% and dollar index to 101.14 the rupee is set to open at 95.86 this morning with RBI continuously protecting the 96.00 levels for the moment.

The RBI Dy. Governor Poonam Gupta was on record to say that Rupee has a fair case to appreciate. On the other hand, S&P, Fitch, ADB and Moody’s raise India’s FY-27 GDP Growth forecast citing stronger than expected economic activity and resilient domestic demand. Most of the projections were closer to 7%.

Exporters may continue to sell nearer to 95.90 levels where RBI is protecting the rupee downside while importers to keep buying dips like one we got on Tuesday at 95.59. Importers need to wait for hedging their imports, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Indonesian Rupiah emerging as the top gainer, rising 0.37% from the previous close. The Japanese Yen also strengthened 0.285%, while the South Korean Won declined 0.336%, making it the weakest performer in the region.

The Philippines Peso slipped 0.172%, while the Chinese Renminbi fell 0.171%. The Malaysian Ringgit and Taiwan Dollar declined 0.191% and 0.22%, respectively. The Singapore Dollar and Thai Baht were largely stable, easing 0.023% and 0.021%.

The dollar clung to a two-month high on Thursday after a strong manufacturing reading reignited inflation fears and rate-hike bets, while a weak Treasury auction sent yields higher across the curve, providing fresh impetus to the US currency.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens lower at 95.83 per dollar; Asian currencies trade mixed
